meta.title: Policy watch
meta.method: Curated, not a feed. An entry is listed only after someone has read its source. verification.level "primary" means checked against the primary document itself; "reported" means taken from a named outlet whose page was read, without checking the primary document. Each primary entry carries the exact source wording it rests on in `evidence`. A topic nobody has checked yet is listed in known_gaps rather than filled from search results. `derived` records a figure computed from the evidence (a sum), and `redline` records a struck and inserted amount that the PDF text runs together.
known_gaps: Local county and city housing questions on the November 3, 2026 ballot: not yet loaded. Each needs checking against the county clerk's ballot notice before it is listed.
Statewide ballot measures for November 3, 2026: not yet loaded.

Housing appointments (checked 2026-09-26 against official pages): listed are the DOLA Executive Director, the Division of Housing Director, CHFA's Executive Director and CEO and its Board Chair, the eight State Housing Board members, and OEDIT's Director of Innovative Funding for Housing Programs. Not listed: a director of the Office of Homeless Initiatives (the Division of Housing's page names the office but no director); a named Proposition 123 program lead at DOLA (DOLA's Proposition 123 pages name only a community support team); and a Governor's senior housing policy adviser (no governor's-office page naming that role was found, and governor.colorado.gov did not respond on 2026-09-26).
Candidates' housing platforms: not yet loaded.
The final 2027–2028 QAP: the QAP entries here are from the third draft, not the adopted plan.

entries.title: Third draft lowers the federal 9% per-project maximum: $1.8M to $1.7M in 2027, then $1.75M in 2028
entries.detail: Section 3.L, Maximum Credit Award. The cap applies to any one project, applicant or affiliate; projects financed with private activity bonds are excluded. The figure struck in the redline is $1.8M. A $1.85M figure that has circulated does not appear in this draft.

evidence.quote: CHFA will accept Applications for no more than $1,800700,000 in 2027 and $1,750,000 in 2028 of the annual federal 9 percent Housing Tax Credit for any one project or any one Applicant
evidence.note: Redline: $1,800,000 struck, $1,700,000 inserted for 2027.

entries.title: Without state gap funds, the maximum stays at $1.8M in both years
entries.detail: Section 3.L.1 keeps the $1.8M cap in 2027 and 2028 when state gap funds are not available to the project under the 3.B.9 pilot.

evidence.quote: Maximum Credit Award if state gap funds are not available under 3.B.9 Pilot Coordinated Funding and Concurrent Awards
Federal Credits No more than $1,800,000 of annual federal 9 percent Housing Tax Credit in 2027 and 2028.

entries.title: New pilot: DOH and OEDIT gap funding offered with the credit award, $74M in 2027
entries.detail: Section 3.B.9. If gap funding is requested in the credit application and the project wins credits, DOH or OEDIT offers a conditional award. 2027: OEDIT $25M in Round One ($40,000 a unit, up to $2.25M) and $19M in Round Two ($30,000 a unit, up to $2.6M); DOH $12M in Round One ($45,000 a unit, up to $2.5M) and $18M in Round Two ($35,000 a unit, up to $3.2M).

evidence.quote: If state gap funding is requested at the time of Housing Tax Credit Application, and the project is awarded credits, a conditional award from either DOH or OEDIT will be offered.

In 2027, OEDIT will pilot a commitment of $25 million for Round One with a fixed loan amount of $40,000 per unit and a maximum of $2.25 million per application. OEDIT will pilot a commitment of $19 million for Round Two with a fixed loan amount of $30,000 per unit and a maximum of $2.6 million per application.

In 2027, DOH will pilot a commitment of $12 million for Round One with a fixed loan or grant amount of $45,000 per unit and a maximum of $2.5 million per application. DOH will pilot a commitment of $18 million for Round Two with a fixed loan or grant amount of $35,000 per unit and a maximum of $3.2 million per application.

entries.title: The same pilot in 2028: $63M from DOH and OEDIT
entries.detail: 2028: OEDIT $18M in Round One ($35,000 a unit, up to $2.25M) and $15M in Round Two ($20,000 a unit, up to $2M); DOH $18M in Round One ($45,000 a unit, up to $2.5M) and $12M in Round Two ($28,000 a unit, up to $2.5M).

evidence.quote: In 2028, OEDIT will pilot a commitment of $18 million for Round One with a fixed loan amount of $35,000 per unit and a maximum of $2.25 million per application. OEDIT will pilot a commitment of $15 million for Round Two with a fixed loan amount of $20,000 per unit and a maximum of $2 million per application.

In 2028, DOH will pilot a commitment of $18 million for Round One with a fixed loan or grant amount of $45,000 per unit and a maximum of $2.5 million per application. DOH will pilot a commitment of $12 million for Round Two with a fixed loan or grant amount of $28,000 per unit and a maximum of $2.5 million per application.

entries.title: Gap terms: OEDIT lends Prop 123 money at 2.5%; DOH lends at 2% or grants
entries.detail: OEDIT funding is Proposition 123 concessionary debt at 2.5% interest, for applications in a Proposition 123 eligible jurisdiction that do not meet DOH eligibility. DOH makes 2% cash-flow loans to for-profit applicants and grants to nonprofits and public housing authorities. The eligibility thresholds are still being edited in the redline.

evidence.quote: If requested, OEDIT funding will be Proposition 123 Concessionary Debt.
and have a 2.5% interest

DOH loans for for-profit applicants will have 2% interest and a term commensurate with senior debt in the application plus six months and will be a cash flow loan. DOH will provide grant funds to nonprofit or public housing authority applicants.

entries.title: The quiet period now covers state gap funders too
entries.detail: Section 3.C.1. During a competitive round, applicants may not contact CHFA staff, board members or state gap funders about a competing project, except to answer staff questions or get technical assistance.

evidence.quote: may not meet with or contact CHFA employees, or Bboard members, or state gap funders about a proposed competitive project(s) competing in the round
evidence.note: Redline: "or state gap funders" is inserted text.

entries.title: Executive Director, Colorado Department of Local Affairs: Maria De Cambra
entries.detail: DOLA lists Maria De Cambra as Executive Director. By statute the Governor appoints the executive director, with the consent of the Senate. The page gives no appointment date.

source.label: Colorado Department of Local Affairs, Leadership

evidence.quote: Executive Director Maria De Cambra
The executive director shall be appointed by the governor, with the consent of the senate, and shall serve at the pleasure of the governor.
evidence.note: Colorado Revised Statutes 2024, Title 24, as published by the Office of Legislative Legal Services: https://leg.colorado.gov/sites/default/files/images/olls/crs2024-title-24.pdf

entries.appointing_authority: Governor, with the consent of the Senate (C.R.S. 24-1-125(1))
relevance: C.R.S. 24-1-125(1) makes the executive director the head of the Department of Local Affairs, which contains the Division of Housing (C.R.S. 24-32-704).

entries.detail: DOLA lists Tyler Jaeckel as Division of Housing Director. By statute the division is headed by the state director of housing, appointed by DOLA's executive director. The page gives no appointment date.

The division shall be headed by the state director of housing appointed by the executive director of the department of local affairs in accordance with section 13 of article XII of the state constitution.
evidence.note: Colorado Revised Statutes 2024, Title 24, as published by the Office of Legislative Legal Services: https://leg.colorado.gov/sites/default/files/images/olls/crs2024-title-24.pdf

entries.agency: Colorado Department of Local Affairs, Division of Housing
entries.appointing_authority: Executive Director of the Department of Local Affairs (C.R.S. 24-32-704(1))
relevance: C.R.S. 24-32-704(1): the state director of housing heads the Division of Housing.

entries.title: Board Chair, Colorado Housing and Finance Authority: Albus Brooks
entries.detail: CHFA lists Albus Brooks as Board Chair, with a board term that expires 07.01.2027. CHFA's leadership page says eight board members are appointed by the Governor and confirmed by the State Senate; it does not say how the chair is chosen.

verification.against: CHFA's board of directors page and its leadership page

evidence.quote:
Albus Brooks
Vice President of Business Development and Public Affairs, Milender White Construction Company
Board Chair
Term expires 07.01.2027.

CHFA is governed by an 11-member board of directors consisting of: the State Auditor, a member of the Governor’s cabinet, a member of the Colorado general assembly, and eight members appointed to four-year terms by the Governor and confirmed by the State Senate.
evidence.note: From https://www.chfainfo.com/about-chfa/leadership.

entries.appointing_authority: Governor, confirmed by the State Senate, for the board seat; CHFA's page does not say who selects the chair
relevance: CHFA's leadership page: the Board of Directors is the governing body of CHFA and is vested with all of CHFA's statutory authority.

entries.title: Director of Innovative Funding for Housing Programs, OEDIT: Hilary Cooper
entries.detail: OEDIT's staff directory lists Hilary Cooper as Director of Innovative Funding for Housing Programs. OEDIT's announcement of the appointment, dated July 11, 2023, says the director oversees implementation of three housing programs, including Proposition 123. The current directory does not restate that assignment.

source.label: Colorado Office of Economic Development and International Trade, Staff

verification.against: OEDIT's staff directory and OEDIT's July 11, 2023 announcement

evidence.quote:
Hilary Cooper
Director of Innovative Funding for Housing Programs
Tuesday, July 11, 2023
evidence.note: The date line of the announcement at https://oedit.colorado.gov/press-release/oedit-announces-former-san-miguel-county-commissioner-as-head-of-new-innovative

evidence.quote: The Business Funding & Incentives Division (BF&I) within the Colorado Office of Economic Development & International Trade (OEDIT) has named Hilary Cooper as Director of Innovative Funding for Housing Programs to support new housing initiatives within OEDIT.
evidence.note: From https://oedit.colorado.gov/press-release/oedit-announces-former-san-miguel-county-commissioner-as-head-of-new-innovative

evidence.quote: She will oversee the implementation of three new housing programs. Proposition 123 supports the development of low-and middle-income, multi-family units through land banking, concessionary debt and equity financing for affordable housing development.

entries.role: Director of Innovative Funding for Housing Programs
entries.agency: Colorado Office of Economic Development and International Trade
entries.appointing_authority: OEDIT Business Funding & Incentives Division (per OEDIT's announcement)
relevance: OEDIT's July 11, 2023 announcement: the director oversees the implementation of Proposition 123, the Middle Income Housing Authority and the Innovative Housing Incentive Program.
